name: RES4SHO cosine and Kumaraswamy two-stage schedules
plain: Same two-stage layout, but each stage is shaped by a function of normalised position rather than distance from a pivot. cosine ignores the pivot and gives each stage a full half-cosine ease, so the step size shrinks towards zero at both ends of each stage and steps bunch around the midpoint sigma as well as the ends. kumaraswamy uses a Kumaraswamy CDF whose exponents come from slope and pivot; the bong layout puts the pivots at the clamp limits (0.95 for stage 1, 0.05 for stage 2). The code notes it is not ComfyUI's beta scheduler. Surprises shared by the whole family: a request for N steps returns N+1 steps (n = N+2 minus one junction value, plus a trailing 0); the split point is the linear midpoint of σ_max..σ_min with 60% of the steps above it, so on SD-style models (σ_max about 14.6) most steps sit above σ≈7.3; slopes are divided by n/40, so the shape changes with step count. Registered with use_ms=True; names already in the scheduler table are skipped, not overwritten.
math:
Symbols: N requested steps; σ_max, σ_min from the model; n = N + 2; m = int(0.6 n); σ_mid = σ_min + 0.5(σ_max − σ_min) (linear midpoint).
Stage 1: k = 0..m−1, pivot p1 = m, slope s1' = s1/max(n/40, 0.1); Stage 2: k = 0..n−m−1, pivot p2 = 0, slope s2' = s2/max(n/40, 0.1).
Each stage: r_k = curve(k; p, s'); r̂_k = (r_k − r_last)/(r_first − r_last); σ_k = end + r̂_k (start − end), stage 1 from σ_max to σ_mid, stage 2 from σ_mid to σ_min.
Output = stage 1 without its last value, stage 2, then 0: N+2 values, i.e. N+1 steps.
t = k/(len−1).
cosine: curve = (1 + cos(π t^{max(s,0.01)}))/2 (pivot unused; slope 1.0, normalised by n/40 like the others).
kumaraswamy: q = clip(p/(len−1), 0.05, 0.95); c = max(5s, 0.1); a = max(c(1−q), 0.01), b = max(c q, 0.01); curve = (1 − t^a)^b (i.e. 1 − Kumaraswamy CDF). Slope 0.20.

props.params: fixed by name; no inputs beyond steps
props.prints: draws an ASCII plot of the schedule to the console on every call
